FRONT_INTRO:
## Before You Begin

You are about to spend one night in a hospital that never lets anyone go.

You don't read this book from front to back. Most sections end with a choice, and each choice sends you to a numbered section. Turn there, read on, choose again.

Some choices will save you. Some will cost you things you can't get back. A few will kill you, and when they do, the book will tell you where to start again.

Your mum has been in theatre since twenty to eleven. You have been her carer for six years. Your sister has just landed from Toronto. And the night nurse doing her rounds is the kindest person you have met in years. She would like to look after you. She would like to look after you for good.

Before you go any further, decide one thing.

Your mum calls you **Bean**, because you were the size of a broad bean on the first scan, and she has never let it go. But who are you to her?

*Her daughter.* Write **DAUGHTER** on your Adventure Sheet.

*Her son.* Write **SON** on your Adventure Sheet.

*Neither word fits, and she has never needed one. Just her kid.* Write **KID** on your Adventure Sheet.

Now choose how you want to play.

**Story Mode.** Don't roll for your scores. Write down **Nerve 9**, **Vigour 20** and **Fortune 9**, which makes your Fear limit 12.

When you are asked to test your Nerve or your Fortune, when something is chasing you, or when you have to fight, choose the outcome you'd like and turn there. (Don't subtract from your Fortune when you choose a Fortune result.) The Night Sister can still write you down, and you can still be frightened past your limit. The hospital plays fair, but it plays.

**Survival Mode.** Roll for your Nerve, Vigour and Fortune as the next pages describe, and play every test, every chase and every fight by the dice. Nothing is guaranteed.

Theatre ends at six. It is 01:40.

Turn to section 1.
FRONT_RULES:
## How the Hospital Works

### Nerve

Your steadiness. In Survival Mode, roll one die and add 6. In Story Mode, it is 9. To test your Nerve, roll two dice: if the total is equal to or under your Nerve, you succeed.

### Vigour

Your body. In Survival Mode, roll two dice and add 12. In Story Mode, it is 20. It can never rise above its starting score. When it reaches 0, you can't go on (see **Checkpoints and death**).

### Fortune

Your luck. In Survival Mode, roll one die and add 6. In Story Mode, it is 9. To test your Fortune, roll two dice: equal to or under it, you are Lucky; over it, you are Unlucky. Either way, subtract 1 from your Fortune afterwards. If your Fortune is 0 or less, you are always Unlucky.

### Fear

Fear starts at 0 and can never fall below 0. Your limit is your Nerve plus 3, which is 12 in Story Mode. If your Fear ever reaches its limit, you stop fighting being looked after: turn straight to {E_ADMITTED}. Check your Fear whenever you gain it.

### The Wristband

Your Adventure Sheet has a hospital wristband with five fields: NAME, DATE OF BIRTH, NEXT OF KIN, WARD and BED. They all start empty.

The Night Sister fills them in. A field goes on every time you accept her care, every time you give the hospital your details, every time you die from the Main Corridor onwards, and every time her round finds you. The book will say: "Fill in 1 more field on your Wristband." Tick one empty field. If the book names the field, tick that one; if it doesn't, tick the next empty one. What counts is how many are filled.

Fields come off only when someone claims you back: when someone who loves you says the true thing, or when Ros cuts one off. The book will say: "Cross off 1 field on your Wristband."

At 3 or more fields, staff recognise a patient, and may stop you.

If 4 fields are filled, the true ending is closed to you: the recovery room won't let a patient visit a patient. If all 5 are filled, you have been admitted: turn straight to {E_ADMITTED}.

### Rounds

Your Adventure Sheet has six boxes for the Night Sister's rounds, 01:00 to 06:00. None of them is ticked when you start.

Tick the next box each time you come back to the Main Corridor from the Old Wing, the Basement or Maternity. The book will say: "Tick one round on your Adventure Sheet." Your first arrival at the Main Corridor, from Level 3, doesn't tick, and neither do deaths. The corridor clock always shows the last box you ticked: it keeps the hospital's time, not yours.

The rounds matter when you reach Ward 0. If you have ticked 4 boxes or fewer, you will be rewarded there. If you have ticked 5, it will cost you 1 field on your Wristband. If you ever tick the sixth box, 06:00, the last round has found you in a bed: turn straight to {E_ADMITTED}.

### Fighting

Each round of a fight, roll two dice and add your Nerve, then do the same for your enemy. Whoever scores higher wounds the other for 2 Vigour. A tie wounds no one: fight another round. When your enemy's Vigour reaches 0, you have won, so read on. If yours reaches 0, you have lost.

### Chases

Some things here can't be fought, only outrun. When something comes after you, the book will tell you to test your Nerve, or, when only luck will save you, your Fortune. Succeed and you get away. Fail and it catches you, and the section says what that costs before you read on.

### Codewords and items

When the book says "Note the codeword SPOKE" or "Note the GLASSES on your Adventure Sheet", write it down. When it tells you to cross one off, cross it off. They remember what you did, even when you'd rather forget.

Codewords are exact: SPOKE is not HELD, and HELD is not MENDED. When a section asks whether you have one, only that word counts.

### Checkpoints and death

Some section numbers are marked with ✈. Whenever you reach one, write its number in the LAST ✈ CHECKPOINT box on your Adventure Sheet.

When you die, the section names where to go back to. Do what it tells you, turn there, and choose again, with the rest of your Adventure Sheet as it was. On Level 3, before you reach the Main Corridor, going back costs nothing. Level 3 deaths cost no field. From the Main Corridor onwards, every death fills in 1 field on your Wristband.

If your Vigour reaches 0, that is a death too. From the Main Corridor onwards, fill in 1 field on your Wristband. Then turn back to the last ✈ section you visited, restore your Vigour to its starting score, and try again.

### Back to the beginning

One ending sends you back to section 1 to begin the night again. If it does, keep DAUGHTER, SON or KID: that never changes. Keep your lore, too: everything you have read, you know.

Cross off everything else. Your Nerve, Vigour, Fortune and Fear return to their starting scores; every codeword and item goes; every round box is cleared. Rub out your Wristband, then fill in 1 field again: the hospital remembers you.

### The Notice

When you find the Night Staff Notice, its rules are printed on your Adventure Sheet. There are seven of them. There used to be eight. Believe them, until you have a reason not to.
